newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA MINISTER VISITS DIAMONDFIELDS MINE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA MINISTER VISITS DIAMONDFIELDS MINE.

text.p: South African Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said on Friday that 22 miners were feared dead after a mudslide at a diamond mine in Free State province.
The miners were crushed in an underground mudslide on Wednesday which followed heavy rains at the Roberts Victor Diamond Mine, owned by Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc .
A total of 34 miners were rescued, four bodies were recovered and another 18 miners were still unaccounted for at the on Friday morning, Maduna said in a statement.
"I sincerely hope that those still unaccounted for will be spared," the minister said, adding he would visit the mine with the government mining engineer Dick Bakker on Friday.
An inquiry would be held to probe the cause of the disaster near Dealesville, some 60 km (38 miles) west of the provincial capital Bloemfontein.

Rescue teams abandoned their search for other survivors on Thursday after it became too dangerous to continue, as mud was still flowing into the mine. Mining officials said there was little hope that other miners would have survived the mud crash.
Seventeen people died in 1994 when a wall burst at a slimes dam at a gold mine at Virginia in Free State province.
